report:
Fresh review after evidence improvements. Reviewed the complete annotation_validation claim, all six ordinary implementation entries, and all five associated ordinary tests. There is no TODO/N/A evidence. Requirements are rejection of malformed/unknown directives, invalid compiler conditions, missing/unused observation expectations, invalid selections, exactly one combined expectation for any type/symbol markers, and validation independent of blessing without silent omission.

annotations.rs parse recognizes only real line-comment directives and exact supported token sequences, rejecting the catch-all and targetless annotations. mod.rs prepare parses all files and compares existence of Type/Symbol markers with observations.is_some(), rejecting both missing and unused observations; expectation_field rejects duplicate assignment. run requires successful preparation before any expectation assertion and has no update-mode bypass. observe.rs rejects out-of-crate markers, incomplete/invalid selected rows, fallible symbol identities and empty type/path selections. source.rs enumerates source expressions for semantic correspondence, types.rs read/complete recursively rejects missing nested type information, and symbols.rs produces explicit errors for missing/ambiguous/unsupported identities rather than silently omitting selections. These three essential helper files now have implementation associations and are included in initial whole-file snapshots. Captured rustc.rs additionally explains the independent compiler marker-matching failure used by the blessing subprocess test; exhaustive compiler matching belongs to compiler_conditions while the common prepare-before-update boundary supplies this claim's update independence.

only_real_line_comment_directives_are_interpreted visibly asserts ignoring marker-like literals/block comments, rejection of targetless ty/sym, malformed slug syntax and unsupported conditions/case, plus valid Unicode placement. expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree rejects a ty marker without observations, an unused observation expectation, and a closing-brace type selection with no expression. symbol_selections_require_paths_and_expectations rejects missing sym observations and a sym target without a path. duplicate_observation_expectations_are_rejected now invokes the public macro with two observations fields and requires the specific duplicate-field panic, covering exactly one combined expectation. The newly associated blessing_edits_the_inline_callsite_and_then_passes_without_updates test runs a disposable fixture in a subprocess with UPDATE_EXPECT=1, asserts a marker-validation failure and byte-identical source, then checks normal mismatch leaves source unchanged, valid blessing edits the authored expectation, and an independent updating-disabled run passes unchanged. This exercises validation independence through run. In conjunction with the inspected single preparation barrier and direct invalid-annotation/selection tests, it establishes the requirement without duplicating subprocess infrastructure or requiring failure injection into every preparation stage.

Executed cargo test -p sage-test-harness --test annotation_validation --test callsite_updates: both tests passed, including child update/no-update invocations. Earlier in this review task, cargo test -p sage-test-harness --lib compile::tests::expectations_and_source_selections_must_agree passed. Other associated unit tests were source-inspected, not rerun by this reviewer. cargo fmt and cargo build succeeded. No production behavior changed: edits add associations and a focused regression test. All previous requested evidence improvements are resolved.
